newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africans seek foreign investors for game parks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africans seek foreign investors for game parks.

text.p: South African tobacco tycoon Anton Rupert is launching a foundation to attract foreign investment for the development of seven trans-frontier wildlife reserves, the head of the foundation said on Friday.

John Hanks, currently director of the South African branch of the Worldwide Fund for Nature (WWF), said the Foundation for Peace Parks in Southern Africa would be formally established in February with a "very generous" contribution from Rupert.
"The idea is to raise a very large sum of money for the seven trans-frontier conservation areas that involve South Africa," Hanks said in a telephone interview.
The proposals would merge South African parks with adjoining land in neighbouring Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Swaziland and Lesotho.
Hanks declined to identify all the parks involved but said one of them was the Kruger National Park, at 20,000 square km the biggest in South Africa.
The World Bank is already studying proposals to join the Kruger Park to a similar-sized area in Mozambique.

"We've already had meetings with World Bank people, we've met with high-level authorities in Mozambique, it has enormous potential in terms of developing a sustainable ecotourism industry and creating jobs of hundreds of people," Hanks said.

"It's got a lot of economic potential for the region. I know of no other industry that can generate the same financial returns on a long-term basis than the development of the right kind of tourism infrastructure," Hanks said.
"I'm optimistic it's going to bring in millions of new money. We've been sounding out people overseas, and the response has been quite staggering."
